rationale: Both role-isolated advisory inputs were present from distinct runs and model families, pinned to the same frozen candidate, and both returned request-changes. No finding carries blocking severity and all ten actionable findings were correctable in this pass, so all were disposed here. Three mattered most. A persistence-length ratio was being read as proof that a single actin filament could bear a mechanical load, when it only places the polymer in a stiffness class; the pack's own source describes the observed core as a cross-linked bundle of about 19 filaments, so the procedure now narrows the choice of polymer and the bundle is named as how the load is met. Two junction routes were over-extended from one adhesion system to a whole location, giving the catenin route to nectins and the integrin-linked-kinase route to every basal integrin including an alpha6beta4 receptor that carries no beta1 subunit; both are corrected and both became distractors, which makes the pairing item test the error a learner actually makes rather than the inversion it tested before. And six load-bearing facts were asserted with no claim record, several of them inherited from earlier lessons of this block, which does not exempt them from the ledger. The maintainer notes for the record that the stiffness finding was missed in his own pre-review read of the same item; the academic reviewer caught it.
dissent: Both reviews returned request-changes, and both verdicts stand as material dissent from the candidate as reviewed. Every finding was incorporated by the maintainer afterwards; no reviewer has seen the repaired text.

Whether the basal surface of a colonic cell carries a second, keratin-linked attachment is not answered by the sources used here. The map draws the beta1 route for that reason and the gap is left visible rather than filled.
conditions: The repaired content is committed first and that commit is stamped as finalCommit, with no teaching-content change afterward.
Strict source preflight and full validation must pass on the final content before merge.
The publication transition is the maintainer's separate act and is not authorised by this decision.
